idiom_name: class ServiceProxy(private val real: ServiceApi) : ServiceApi by real
implementation_notes: Kotlin compiles the classic structure: the by clause in the supertype list stores the delegate and makes the compiler generate forwarding members for the whole interface, so equivalence is guaranteed by the compiler rather than by review, and only the members that need control are written as overrides. The documentation calls this zero boilerplate and states two consequences that matter here: a member overridden in the delegating class is not seen by the delegate's own methods, and the delegate is fixed at construction. For a wire service the framework form is a JVM gRPC ServerInterceptor, which the same file can use.
pitfalls: Self-calls inside the delegate bypass the proxy: an override is not used when the delegate calls another of its own interface methods, so interception is not transitive.
Delegation is bound to one instance at construction; use a provider or a delegating property to a var if the service can be replaced.
Suspending interface members are forwarded as ordinary members, but a proxy that switches dispatchers or wraps calls in runBlocking silently changes the suspension contract.

variants.name: JVM gRPC ServerInterceptor for a wire service
variants.idiom_name: io.grpc.ServerInterceptor in front of the generated service
variants.implementation_notes: On the wire the equivalent interface is the generated service base class and the interception point is the io.grpc ServerInterceptor, which sees the method descriptor, the call metadata and the next handler, so tenant checks, authentication, tracing and error mapping are applied around the service. Kotlin uses the same gRPC-java API as Java, so one interceptor protects Kotlin and Java services in the same process, and the client-side counterpart does the same for outgoing calls.
pitfalls: The listener returned by startCall must be forwarded (or wrapped): dropping it cancels the call with a status the client cannot explain.
Metadata keys are the only per-call channel for identity and deadlines; shared mutable state in the interceptor races across concurrent RPCs.
Interceptors still run on gRPC threads, so blocking work there stalls unrelated RPCs even in a coroutine-based service.
